channel.title: Searchscope Blog
channel.description: Writing on search systems, algorithm updates, AI search and search data.

item.title: Page Experience
item.description: See which technical issues matter, whether Google has indexed the page, and how it performs. Page Experience brings the checks together without making you join the dots across three tools.
item.author: noreply@searchscope.io (Ray Olaibi)

item.title: Names you weren't getting credit for
item.description: AI engines rarely use a brand name in exactly the same way every time. Searchscope finds missed name variants and lets you approve them before they affect your reporting.
item.author: noreply@searchscope.io (Ray Olaibi)

item.title: All six AI engines, live
item.description: ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Claude and Gemini now run side by side. The differences between them are often more useful than the combined score.
item.author: noreply@searchscope.io (Ray Olaibi)

item.title: The Content Planner
item.description: The Content Planner builds an SEO and PR plan from the data already in Searchscope, then sends approved pieces into Content Studio with the context intact.
item.author: noreply@searchscope.io (Ray Olaibi)

item.title: Send any strategist reply to Content Studio
item.description: Send a Strategic Advisor reply into Content Studio without losing the conversation that produced it. The useful context comes with the task.
item.author: noreply@searchscope.io (Ray Olaibi)

item.title: A rebuilt AI visibility overview
item.description: See how often your brand is named and cited, how much share of voice it holds, and where it appears inside the answer. Every metric shows the numbers behind it.
item.author: noreply@searchscope.io (Ray Olaibi)

item.title: Worksheets
item.description: Turn any analyzer workspace into a working sheet with status, priority, notes and batch recommendations. Preview the output before you run it across the full set.
item.author: noreply@searchscope.io (Ray Olaibi)

item.title: Prompt suggestions from your own search data
item.description: Build AI tracking prompts from the searches already bringing people to your site, then keep the ones that reflect real demand rather than a guessed prompt list.
item.author: noreply@searchscope.io (Ray Olaibi)

item.title: A demo on every page
item.description: Seventeen narrated walkthroughs now sit on the screens they explain. When a page has a demo, you can watch it without leaving the work you're doing.
item.author: noreply@searchscope.io (Ray Olaibi)

item.title: SEO is now an operating system
item.description: SEO still gets managed like a sequence of projects, even though search changes every week. The better model is continuous: read what changed, decide what matters, then act while the signal is still useful.
item.author: noreply@searchscope.io (Ray Olaibi)

item.title: What AI Overviews change about visibility
item.description: Rankings still matter, but they no longer tell you enough on their own. AI Overviews can take the click above you, or cite you when you don't rank in the traditional results at all.
item.author: noreply@searchscope.io (Ray Olaibi)

item.title: Cannibalization is a data problem
item.description: Cannibalization isn't something you should diagnose because two pages look similar. The useful signal is in query-by-page search data, where multiple URLs are competing for the same intent.
item.author: noreply@searchscope.io (Ray Olaibi)

item.title: Reading demand vs. your share
item.description: Rankings show where you sit. Demand against share shows where the commercial headroom is. High demand with low captured share is usually the part of the site worth looking at first.
item.author: noreply@searchscope.io (Ray Olaibi)

item.title: The co-pilot model for search teams
item.description: AI is useful for the parts of search work that involve reading, checking and sorting at scale. The strategist should still own the judgment, priorities and decisions that follow.
item.author: noreply@searchscope.io (Ray Olaibi)
